jobs.title: Geospatial Engineer – Multiple Positions at Junior/Mid/Senior Levels
jobs.description:
Overview

Geospatial Engineer – Multiple Positions at Junior/Mid/Senior Levels

NV5 Geospatial (NV5G) is actively recruiting qualified and cleared Geospatial Engineers to support national security client sites in the Northern Virginia and St. Louis, MO areas. Candidates will support mission-critical Intelligence Community and Department of War projects by designing, analyzing, and supporting geospatial data, systems, and workflows. This role leverages GIS expertise and Esri technologies to deliver high-quality geospatial products, analysis, and user support in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. A Top Secret Clearance with SCI eligibility or an active TS/SCI are required conditions of employment.

Work Environment

Location: St. Louis, MO Area (St. Louis, MO and/or St. Charles, MO)
Travel up to 15% of the time

At NV5, we are a collaboration of intelligent, innovative thinkers who care for each other, our communities, and the environment. We value both heart and head, the diversity of our people, and their experiences because that is how we continue to grow as a leader in our industry and expand our individual and collective potential.

NV5 is a global technology solutions and consulting services company with a workforce of over 4,500 professionals in more than 100 offices worldwide. NV5’s continued growth has been spurred through strategic investments in firms with unique capabilities to help current and future customers solve the world’s toughest problems. The NV5 family brings together talent across a wide range of markets and fields, including Professional Engineers, Professional Land Surveyors, Architects, Photogrammetrists, GIS Professionals, Software Developers, IT, Project Management Professionals, and more.

Responsibilities

Collect, analyze, validate, and manage geospatial data using GIS, remote sensing, and GPS tools
Design, build, maintain, and test geospatial databases and enterprise geodatabases
Perform spatial analysis and GIS processing using ArcGIS and related Esri products
Develop and maintain automated workflows and scripts using Python and SQL
Produce maps, web maps, and visualizations to support analysis and decision making
Integrate geospatial data with other datasets to generate actionable insights
Provide technical support and troubleshooting for GIS users and systems
Support data automation, migration, and database development efforts
Coordinate tasks with project and technical managers
Document processes, results, and customer interactions

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

US citizenship with Active or Current (within two years of active) Top Secret Security Clearance with SCI eligibility
Bachelor’s degree in Geography, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), geospatial engineering, computer scient or a related field
2+ years of professional experience using GIS technologies
Knowledge of Windows environments
Proficiency with Esri products (ArcGIS Desktop, Enterprise, and Online)
Experience with spatial analysis, GIS workflows, and database development
Working knowledge of relational databases (Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL)
Strong analytical, problem solving, and communication skills
Ability to manage priorities and work effectively in a team environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in technical support or customer facing GIS roles
Experience with data conversion or migration
Knowledge of Linux and UNIX environments
Familiarity with web mapping and remote sensing tools
Proficiency in Python scripting and SQL
GIS certifications

Clearance Requirement

Active/Current Top Secret Clearance with SCI Eligibility

jobs.title: Geospatial Intelligence Departmental Requirements Officer
jobs.description:
PotomacWave is looking for a Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) Departmental Requirements Officer (DRO) to join our team supporting a Federal client in Washington, DC. The individual supporting this position shall provide GEOINT national technical means and commercial collection requirement systems expertise and support. The individual shall be responsible for assisting in the planning, organizing of integrated, GEOINT collection strategies using complex, coherent, and systematic intelligence collection campaigns employing national, and theater assets against nuclear and energy-related targets world-wide.

Responsibilities

Write, review, and submit GEOINT collection requirements in support of single and all source IN analysts
Provide expert GEOINT collection management and requirements analysis on assigned target areas.
Develop and present intelligence collection management strategies and approaches.
Work effectively as a member of a diverse team, accepting and giving effective feedback, and collaborating with other collection managers across the Intelligence Community (IC).
Coordinate client GEOINT requirements within the GEOINT Requirements Subcommittee structure.
Participate in reviews and assessments of current intelligence tools, processes, tactics, techniques, and procedures.
Use GEOINT databases and query tools to develop reports.
Populate and update national and local GEOINT databases and web pages.
Conduct strategic collection planning and assessments of the effectiveness of GEOINT collection.
Write, review, and submit GEOINT collection requirements.
Monitors current intelligence of specified targets.

Qualifications

Minimum of eight (8) years of experience in GEOINT collection management and/or analysis and production at the tactical, strategic, or national level required.
A strong technical background and understanding of GEOINT tasking, collection, processing, exploitation, and dissemination requirements.
Demonstrated experience in GEOINT intelligence collection requirement management environment to include training and expert knowledge of the GEOINT Information Management Services (GIMS) and proficiency in a wide array of GEOINT NTM and commercial collection requirement systems.
Knowledge of theater, and national intelligence collection platforms and ISR integration strategies; and knowledge of theater and national intelligence requirements processes.
Knowledge of, and skill in applying advanced technical collection planning concepts, principles, practices, laws, regulations, methods, and techniques to include domestic imagery and coalition partner processes, rules, and regulations.
Knowledge of IC GEOINT capabilities and accesses, strengths, and weaknesses of specific technical sensors/platforms sources in the area of GEOINT.
Ability to provide general hands-on instruction to federal analysts on a wide variety of GEOINT products, systems, and tool sets.
Position requires a Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited college in a related discipline.
The selection of an individual for this position may be conditioned upon his or her successful completion of a counterintelligence-scope polygraph examination.
Must have an active TS clearance or DOE Q

Salary range $80,000 - $115,000

jobs.description:
Posting Details

Position Information

Job Description

The Wildlife Ecology Laboratory ( WEL )
at Tennessee State University ( TSU )
is seeking a post-doctoral research associate to utilize environmental DNA as an early screening tool for aquatic invasive species in National Forests throughout the southeast United States. In addition to refining molecular approaches to screen for aquatic invasive species, the project will aim to compare eDNA screening approaches to traditional aquatic survey methods. The postdoc will work collaboratively with researchers from the USDA Forest Service Southern Research Station and Clemson University and will be expected to lead research efforts related to sample processing and post-processing of genome-scale bioinformatics data. The successful candidate will be expected to assist with mentoring graduate and undergraduate students in the WEL . In addition to the primary project responsibilities, there will be opportunities to assist with other ongoing wildlife research projects.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants must hold a PhD in a relevant field and have a demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications, including at least one first author publication. Required skillsets include effective writing and quantitative skills, and prior experience with molecular approaches, including quantitative PCR , metabarcoding, and post-processing of genome-scale bioinformatics data. Other preferred skillsets include proficiency with the R statistical analysis platform and prior experience with occupancy and species distribution models.

Special Instructions to Applicants

Employment is contingent upon successfully completing a criminal background check as mandated by Tennessee State University.

Official transcripts for positions which require a post-secondary undergraduate degree, advanced degree and/or certification must be presented upon hire.

An unofficial transcript may be attached in the “Transcript” section.

You will be required to provide names and contact information for three references during your application to the posting. If you are the recommended candidate for the position, our online hiring system will automatically generate solicitation for these letters using contact information you provided.

jobs.title: Environmental Health & Safety Manager
jobs.description:
Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Summary

Job Description

Teledyne Relays (a business unit of Teledyne Defense Electronics, LLC) is a manufacturer of Electromechanical Relays, Solid State Relays, Power Controllers, RF COAX Switches and RF Matrix switching systems. The primary manufacturing facilities are located in the United States. We are a vertically integrated manufacturing and design company with major operations in Southern California.

Teledyne Relays’ mission, vision, and value statements have never really changed in principle since 1963. Dedication to every employee and client’s success; Innovation that matters - for our company and for the world; Trust and personal responsibility in all relationships – Teledyne Relays is EveryWhereYouLook!

Core Competencies

Environmental Management Systems (EMS/HSMS)
Cal-OSHA Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP)
Hazardous Waste Management & Tiered Permitting
Regulatory Reporting (EPA, CalEPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, Cal OSHA, LACSD, CDPH-RHB, LARWQCB, LACFD)
X-ray and Radiation Protection Program
Incident Investigation & Root Cause Analysis
Ergonomic Assessments & Safety Training
Wastewater & Stormwater Compliance
SDS Management & Hazardous Materials Control
Facilities & Utilities Management (HVAC, Clean Rooms, Cryogenics)
Preventive Maintenance Planning

Responsibilities

Provide direction and technical support to department staff responsible for EMS/HSMS compliance
Develop and implement EMS/HSMS programs ensuring compliance with regulations
Organize and update Cal-OSHA IIPP for proactive safety measures, including regular review of the following H&S programs:
Work area inspection & ergonomic assessments
Job Hazard Analysis
Machine Guarding
Lock out / Tag out
Conduct audits of hazardous waste, stormwater, wastewater, and air emissions, X-ray and radiation programs
Manage 22+ EHS permits/licenses, renewals, postings, and compliance documentation
Submit regulatory reports to CalEPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, OSHA, and other agencies
Coordinate incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions
Direct safety training and verify competency through testing
Maintain hazardous waste records, manifests, contingency plans, and SDS library
Support wastewater treatment system and environmental operating procedures

Direct Facilities, Maintenance and Production programs for HVAC, clean rooms, lighting, compressed air systems, cryogenics, construction, plumbing, building interior & exterior and grounds

Manage preventive maintenance logs for production equipment, minimizing downtime

Qualifications

Minimum seven (7) years related experience in Environmental, Health & Safety management
Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering or Industrial Engineering
Must be a US citizen
Skilled in mathematics and chemistry, with computer proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.).
Ability to partner with and effectively communicates to Teledyne Relays management and supervisory staff

In our efforts to maintain a safe and drug-free workplace, Teledyne Relays requires that candidates complete a satisfactory background check and pass a drug screen prior to employment.
Due to the type of work at the facility and certain access restrictions, successful applicants must be a "US Person" (US Citizens, US Nationals, lawful permanent residents, asylees or refugees).

Please note the salary range posted below is a general guideline for this job level and location. When extending an offer, a variety of factors are considered such as responsibilities of the position, relevant education and experience, certifications, knowledge and skills.

Salary Range

$96,600.00-$128,800.000

The anticipated salary range listed for this role is only an estimate. Actual compensation for successful candidates is carefully determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, location, education/training, work experience, key skills, and type of position.

jobs.description:
Company Description
Prism Specialty Restoration provides residential and commercial specialty contents restoration, supporting homeowners, businesses, contractors, and insurance professionals. The company focuses on restoring electronics, art, documents, and textiles using safety-focused, proven processes. Prism delivers consistent quality, cost-effective outcomes, and turnaround times that align with claims and broader restoration timelines. The team prioritizes transparency, clear communication, and documented restoration from pickup through delivery. Every item is treated with care and urgency to reduce downtime and help customers return to normal as quickly as possible.
Role Description
The Document Restoration Management role is a full-time, on-site position based in Indianapolis, IN. This role oversees the end-to-end restoration process for damaged or at-risk documents, including intake, assessment, cataloging, and tracking throughout restoration. Day-to-day responsibilities include coordinating document handling and storage, supervising restoration techniques such as drying, cleaning, and digitization, and ensuring accurate documentation of all work performed. The individual in this role will collaborate with field teams, clients, and insurance partners to provide updates, manage timelines, and help resolve questions about scope and status. The role also involves monitoring quality standards, enforcing safety and confidentiality protocols, and identifying process improvements to enhance efficiency and client experience.
Qualifications

Document restoration and preservation skills, including handling sensitive records, applying appropriate drying and cleaning techniques, and understanding basic archival or records management principles.
Operational and project coordination skills, such as workflow planning, task prioritization, inventory tracking, and schedule management in a fast-paced restoration environment.
Attention to detail and quality control skills, including accurate data entry, meticulous recordkeeping, and the ability to review work for completeness and compliance with company standards.
Customer service and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear updates to clients and insurance partners, explain processes, and address inquiries in a professional, empathetic manner.
Safety, confidentiality, and compliance awareness, including adherence to company safety protocols, secure handling of confidential or sensitive documents, and respect for regulatory and privacy requirements.
Basic technical skills, such as using office software, scanners, and other equipment related to document restoration and digitization.
Ability to work on-site in a physical environment, including standing, lifting, and moving boxes or equipment as needed, with a focus on safe work practices.
Previous experience in restoration, records management, or a related field is beneficial; a high school diploma or equivalent is required, and further education or certifications in restoration or archival work are an advantage.

Teledyne Relays (a business unit of Teledyne Defense Electronics, LLC) is a manufacturer of Electromechanical Relays, Solid State Relays, Power Controllers, RF COAX Switches and RF Matrix switching systems. The primary manufacturing facilities are located in the United States. We are a vertically integrated manufacturing and design company with major operations in Southern California.

Teledyne Relays’ mission, vision, and value statements have never really changed in principle since 1963. Dedication to every employee and client’s success; Innovation that matters - for our company and for the world; Trust and personal responsibility in all relationships – Teledyne Relays is EveryWhereYouLook!

Core Competencies

Environmental Management Systems (EMS/HSMS)
Cal-OSHA Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP)
Hazardous Waste Management & Tiered Permitting
Regulatory Reporting (EPA, CalEPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, Cal OSHA, LACSD, CDPH-RHB, LARWQCB, LACFD)
X-ray and Radiation Protection Program
Incident Investigation & Root Cause Analysis
Ergonomic Assessments & Safety Training
Wastewater & Stormwater Compliance
SDS Management & Hazardous Materials Control
Facilities & Utilities Management (HVAC, Clean Rooms, Cryogenics)
Preventive Maintenance Planning

Responsibilities

Provide direction and technical support to department staff responsible for EMS/HSMS compliance
Develop and implement EMS/HSMS programs ensuring compliance with regulations
Organize and update Cal-OSHA IIPP for proactive safety measures, including regular review of the following H&S programs:
Work area inspection & ergonomic assessments
Job Hazard Analysis
Machine Guarding
Lock out / Tag out
Conduct audits of hazardous waste, stormwater, wastewater, and air emissions, X-ray and radiation programs
Manage 22+ EHS permits/licenses, renewals, postings, and compliance documentation
Submit regulatory reports to CalEPA, DTSC, SCAQMD, OSHA, and other agencies
Coordinate incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions
Direct safety training and verify competency through testing
Maintain hazardous waste records, manifests, contingency plans, and SDS library
Support wastewater treatment system and environmental operating procedures

Direct Facilities, Maintenance and Production programs for HVAC, clean rooms, lighting, compressed air systems, cryogenics, construction, plumbing, building interior & exterior and grounds

Manage preventive maintenance logs for production equipment, minimizing downtime

Qualifications

Minimum seven (7) years related experience in Environmental, Health & Safety management
Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering or Industrial Engineering
Must be a US citizen
Skilled in mathematics and chemistry, with computer proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.).
Ability to partner with and effectively communicates to Teledyne Relays management and supervisory staff

new_jobs.title: Document Restoration Management
new_jobs.description:
Company Description
Prism Specialty Restoration provides residential and commercial specialty contents restoration, supporting homeowners, businesses, contractors, and insurance professionals. The company focuses on restoring electronics, art, documents, and textiles using safety-focused, proven processes. Prism delivers consistent quality, cost-effective outcomes, and turnaround times that align with claims and broader restoration timelines. The team prioritizes transparency, clear communication, and documented restoration from pickup through delivery. Every item is treated with care and urgency to reduce downtime and help customers return to normal as quickly as possible.
Role Description
The Document Restoration Management role is a full-time, on-site position based in Indianapolis, IN. This role oversees the end-to-end restoration process for damaged or at-risk documents, including intake, assessment, cataloging, and tracking throughout restoration. Day-to-day responsibilities include coordinating document handling and storage, supervising restoration techniques such as drying, cleaning, and digitization, and ensuring accurate documentation of all work performed. The individual in this role will collaborate with field teams, clients, and insurance partners to provide updates, manage timelines, and help resolve questions about scope and status. The role also involves monitoring quality standards, enforcing safety and confidentiality protocols, and identifying process improvements to enhance efficiency and client experience.
Qualifications

Document restoration and preservation skills, including handling sensitive records, applying appropriate drying and cleaning techniques, and understanding basic archival or records management principles.
Operational and project coordination skills, such as workflow planning, task prioritization, inventory tracking, and schedule management in a fast-paced restoration environment.
Attention to detail and quality control skills, including accurate data entry, meticulous recordkeeping, and the ability to review work for completeness and compliance with company standards.
Customer service and communication skills, with the ability to provide clear updates to clients and insurance partners, explain processes, and address inquiries in a professional, empathetic manner.
Safety, confidentiality, and compliance awareness, including adherence to company safety protocols, secure handling of confidential or sensitive documents, and respect for regulatory and privacy requirements.
Basic technical skills, such as using office software, scanners, and other equipment related to document restoration and digitization.
Ability to work on-site in a physical environment, including standing, lifting, and moving boxes or equipment as needed, with a focus on safe work practices.
Previous experience in restoration, records management, or a related field is beneficial; a high school diploma or equivalent is required, and further education or certifications in restoration or archival work are an advantage.
